findings.title: Discarded excess shard-aware connection never decrements total_connections
findings.claim: This branch drops an already inc_total_connections()-counted Connection and retries on the regular port, leaving the one remaining hole in the decrement invariant the PR establishes elsewhere; under source-port-rewriting NAT the counter inflates without bound.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections loops fetch_sub(1) instead of one bulk fetch_sub(count)
findings.claim: Since excess_connection_limit() is 10 * nr_shards, clearing the excess pool on a 64-shard node costs ~640 atomic RMWs where a single fetch_sub(count) would do; needs a bulk helper on Metrics/metrics_noop.

findings.title: No Drop impl for PoolRefiller leaks connection count on pool teardown
findings.claim: Tearing a pool down (node removed, session dropped) leaks the count of every connection still in conns/excess_connections; this is the same accounting class the PR is closing but is pre-existing/out of scope and not covered by the new tests.

findings.title: many_connections test failure is environmental, not a regression
findings.claim: The many_connections test fails under cargo test, but it fails identically on main because the sandbox has no route to the simulated address, so the failure is environmental rather than a regression from this PR.

findings.title: --no-default-features build/test passes; metrics feature gating on new code is correct
findings.claim: The crate builds and passes tests with --no-default-features, confirming the #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] gating on the new tests/helpers is correct.

findings.title: clippy clean for lib/lib-tests; benches/benchmark.rs failure is pre-existing
findings.claim: cargo clippy is clean for lib and lib-tests; the benches/benchmark.rs failure needs --cfg scylla_unstable and is pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

findings.title: New ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant is safe to add
findings.claim: The enum is #[non_exhaustive] with no exhaustive matches in-tree, and size_of::<ConnectionError>() is unchanged at 112 bytes on both branches, staying under the result_large_err clippy threshold, so the new variant is safe.

findings.title: New maybe_reshard decrement cannot double-count with remove_connection's decrement
findings.claim: Cleared connections are no longer findable by ptr_eq, so the decrement in remove_connection is skipped in that path, preventing double-counting with the new maybe_reshard decrement.

findings.title: Reordering keyspace check ahead of maybe_reshard/shard_aware_port only delays discovery by one round-trip
findings.claim: Moving the keyspace check ahead of maybe_reshard/shard_aware_port only delays sharder discovery by one round-trip and actually avoids wiping the pool for a connection that is then discarded.

findings.title: evt.requested_shard survives the USE round-trip so block_advanced_shard_awareness still fires
findings.claim: evt.requested_shard survives the USE round-trip, so block_advanced_shard_awareness still fires correctly after the reordering.

findings.title: full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics test is deterministic
findings.claim: The test is deterministic because the initial start_filling opens zero extra connections, since the pool is already full for PerShard(1).
